name: Open Atlas
subtitle: Knowledge · institutions · commons
question: How can a shared knowledge commons grow without losing consent or maintainability?
context: A fictional federation of a public library, two research labs and a civic archive maintains openly reusable climate-adaptation material. Their memberships overlap but their permissions do not. Volunteer time is pledged and finite. The federation must choose between deeper verification and wider reuse; unpublished personal records cannot be traded for reach.
authority: Open Atlas stewardship council; originating institutions retain publication rights and participants retain consent rights.
principles: No private personal record may be exposed.
Consent is specific, revocable and separate from institutional membership.
Do not create a maintenance burden above the present allocation.
Preserve open reuse and the ability to fork without central permission.

scopes.name: Open Atlas federation
scopes.description: An 18-month shared program has $1.2 million, bounded volunteer pledges and independent institutional commitments.

scopes.name: Public library
scopes.description: Hosts openly licensed materials and assists contributors. Hosting does not confer rights over unpublished records.

scopes.name: Research partnership
scopes.description: Two independent labs validate claims. Their reviewers also contribute to the archive; the same pledged hours cannot be allocated twice.

scopes.name: Civic archive
scopes.description: Holds adaptation records and unpublished oral histories. Only the specifically consented collection can enter the commons.

scopes.name: Contributor assembly
scopes.description: Contributors belong to several institutions but retain individual publication rights. Neither a lab nor the council can override withdrawal.

objectives.label: Reusable materials
objectives.description: Materials with an open license, usable metadata and an exportable file. Items are counted once across the selected work packages.

objectives.label: Verified claims
objectives.description: Share of the reference collection with a traceable evidence check. Forecast changes are percentage-point proxies, not guarantees of truth.

objectives.label: Rights resolved
objectives.description: Share of the reference collection with explicit reuse rights and a withdrawal route. A license alone does not establish participant consent.

objectives.label: Private records exposed
objectives.description: Protected limit on exposure of unpublished personal records. Aggregate openness cannot compensate for even one exposure.

objectives.label: Maintenance burden
objectives.description: Estimated recurring work after the program. Volunteer pledges cover program delivery; they do not silently absorb future maintenance.

source.title: Grant award · synthetic
source.author: Mina Sol
source.excerpt: The 18-month grant commits $1.2 million to federation work. Future fundraising is excluded from available funding.

claims.label: Opt-in volunteer time

source.title: Pledge reconciliation · synthetic
source.author: Tess Okoro
source.excerpt: Named, opt-in pledges total 2,400 hours after removing duplicate pledges across institutions. Contributors may withdraw unworked time.

claims.dissent: About 1,000 hours depend on a university term timetable that has not been confirmed.

source.title: Partner letters · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: The library, labs and archive commit 800 paid hours for this program. The same staff listed in multiple letters were counted once.

source.title: Hosting allocation · synthetic
source.author: Dara Lin
source.excerpt: Partners reserve 20 TB including required replicated copies. Unfunded personal drives are not federation infrastructure.

source.title: Participant permission register · synthetic
source.author: Tess Okoro
source.excerpt: 180 record-specific provisional permissions are active. Openly licensed public reference material uses a separate rights review; no silent personal-record release is assumed.

claims.label: Verification lead

source.title: Review calendar · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: The labs offer a four-month evidence review after catalog reconciliation. This relies on two named reviewers completing a separate public-health study.

claims.dissent: The current study could extend the queue to sixteen months.

source.title: Translation pilot estimate · synthetic
source.author: Dara Lin
source.excerpt: At the working response ratio of 0.8, translated bundles are expected to add 180 reusable items. Pilot readers have not yet checked technical accuracy.

source.title: Reviewer sample · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: A small sample suggests a 0.9 response ratio, modeled as a 20-point increase in verified claims. Ambiguous claims must retain their contested status after review.

interventions.title: Reconcile the public catalog
interventions.mechanism: Deduplicate already-public materials, trace licenses and produce a shared exportable catalog before dependent work.

interventions.title: Review the reference claims
interventions.mechanism: Check the reconciled collection against dated evidence, retaining disagreement and provenance. Verification is a bounded review, not a declaration of universal truth.

interventions.title: Translate reusable bundles
interventions.mechanism: Translate distinct public technical materials after catalog reconciliation. Reader validation limits modeled reach; no personal records enter this package.

interventions.title: Resolve participant permissions
interventions.mechanism: Review 100 provisional permissions with contributors, separate private material from public files and establish an accessible withdrawal path.

interventions.title: Release the consented archive
interventions.mechanism: Publish a distinct permitted collection after catalog and consent review, with replicated files and no private-record exposure.

interventions.title: Publish a portable fork kit
interventions.mechanism: Package verified public material, schemas and offline tooling so independent institutions can reuse and leave the federation without asking central permission.

interventions.title: Import the entire archive
interventions.mechanism: A proposed bulk release would include 20 unpublished personal records and unresolved rights. Its apparent reach is inadmissible under the privacy protection.

strategies.name: Rights and evidence
strategies.thesis: Resolve publication rights and verify the existing collection before seeking scale. Leave capacity for contributors who withdraw.

strategies.name: Portable commons
strategies.thesis: Make reviewed public knowledge reusable across independent institutions. Favor portability and lower maintenance over expanding the personal archive.

strategies.name: Publish everything
strategies.thesis: Test the tempting reach-maximizing portfolio against volunteer pledges, institutional allocations, maintenance and private-record protection.

shocks.name: Pledges withdrawn
shocks.description: The university timetable changes and contributors withdraw 1,000 unworked hours. No agent may assume free replacement labor.

shocks.name: Evidence review delayed
shocks.description: Reviewers extend the public-health study. Verification takes sixteen months after catalog work; the dependent fork kit misses the program horizon.
